note: New 851-line JobLifecycleService mixes genuinely independent change reasons in one class: DB-backed job/sandbox lifecycle (create/close/delete/archive), GitHub PR polling and state application (pollPrClosures, applyGithubPrState, closeJobPullRequest), repo onboarding bookkeeping (markRepoOnboarded, tryRevalidateAccess), host filesystem dir cleanup, and liveness probing. The pollPrClosures/applyGithubPrState PR-sync block changes with GitHub API and wake-funnel requirements, not with sandbox provisioning. God-class creation.

StimulusStoreService is primarily a cohesive inbound-stimulus persistence service (record/lease/deliver/chat+event rows), but it also owns findOwningJobByBranch/findOwningJobByPrNumber — job-ownership resolution queries over JobEntity that change with job-routing rules, not with the stimulus store schema. Modest but real mixed responsibility introduced at creation.

E2eHarness is an intentional e2e orchestrator: boot the app (with fakes), seed a tenant, run three scenarios, record steps. Orchestration that intentionally composes responsibilities is a named exception, so no new concern is warranted. Concern stays below the finding threshold.

LocalGitService is a cohesive low-level git adapter: every method shells out to git or manages locks around git operations. Security scanning (scanBranchForForbidden) is still a git-content query. One reason to change: how Atlas talks to git. Creation of a cohesive subject is not an introduced mix.

OnboardingService mixes repo connection/validation lifecycle (connectRepo, revalidateRepo, disconnectRepo), org onboarding status/activation (status, tryActivate, nextStep), LLM key probing via a live ChatAnthropic call (validateLlmKey), and GitHub webhook registration/pruning (ensureRepoWebhook, ensureWebhooksForActiveRepos). Webhook plumbing and LLM-credential validation each change independently of onboarding flow. New god-ish service.

WorkspaceService composes repositories and services to deliver workspace/job operations; it is close to intentional orchestration/facade (an exception). Still, it directly performs launch-scope resolution and job/workspace deletion sequencing rather than only delegating, so the concern is middling, not a confident violation.

SandboxService mixes pod lifecycle orchestration (ensureReady/teardown/reap) with detailed Kubernetes pod-spec construction (buildPodSpec: volumes, env, securityContext, init containers) and registry digest resolution over HTTP (resolveDesiredImage). The pod-spec schema and registry protocol are independent reasons to change from lease/reap lifecycle.

PlanReviewService mixes review orchestration (run/resume/retry a Codex review) with review-row persistence schema (persistRow/resume-count semantics, thread-group bookkeeping via ensurePlanReviewThread/maxOrdinal) and filesystem spec hashing (hashSpecs walks the context dir). Persistence model and file hashing change independently of review flow.

GithubPrService is a cohesive GitHub API client: every method is an HTTP call to GitHub plus its rate-limit/ETag-cache machinery, which exists to serve those calls. One reason to change: the GitHub API surface Atlas consumes. Not a violation.

SandboxManager is largely container lifecycle (attach/teardown/reap/probe), but also owns host-directory layout and path policy (contextDirHost/playgroundDirHost/draftUploadsDirHost/brainTranscriptProjectsDir plus cacheMountBinds path mapping) and secret file materialization (writeGithubTokenFile, kickMcpHubRefresh config write). Host path conventions and credential delivery change independently of container lifecycle.

EngineCore duplicates two full engine integrations in one class: runClaude (~450 lines of stream protocol handling, circuit breaker, hold timers, usage accounting, session-limit detection) and runCodex (thread management, item mapping, usage aggregation), plus auth resolution, home provisioning and client caching. The Claude and Codex integrations change independently; the class is a two-engine god object despite delegating helpers.
EntityTaskEventSink does one thing: persist task CRUD with dependency edges to TypeORM, with per-scope serialization. Tightly cohesive implementation of a single business capability.

App (TUI composition root) was edited only cosmetically: doc comments removed, a DraftReader type alias applied, and the draft lookup hoisted to a const. No responsibility added or removed; the mix (whatever it was) is materially unchanged.

JsonlThreadStore refactor extracted the persistence machinery into focused modules (thread-store-fields, thread-store-mutations, thread-store-history, listing, meta): rewind/compact/summarise/fork and writePlacement/updateMeta are now thin delegations to named operations. The class is now a facade over cohesive helpers; the previous in-class mix of history rewriting, meta mutation and placement logic is gone from the scope. Under the scoping rule the subject is scope.after, and the focus question is ignored for resolved impact.
